properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): an argument of the wrong JSON type is refused with serde's bare "failed to deserialize parameters: invalid type: …", naming neither the tool nor the field, on every tool, not only external_dependency. The 2026-09-11 interception rewrites two serde phrasings, missing field and unknown field, and its wire gate probes only those two. The door names the tool only on exit 1, and this refusal exits 2
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-02, triaging art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02, tool friction 1. Triage agent C, dev_reflow2 hub.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "`external_dependency` with a string where a list is expected → `failed to deserialize parameters: invalid type: string "…", expected a sequence`: names neither the tool nor the field."

② PRECEDENT:
- epoch:a-missing-argument-names-the-tool-and-what-it-wants (2026-09-11) fixed the "missing field" phrasing and revived the dead "unknown field" one, and pinned both with tools/refusal_speaks.py.
- fact:the-first-real-usage-report-classed-four-of-five-refusals-as-other (2026-09-12) met this EXACT phrasing ("invalid type: string … expected a sequence", on record_finding steps and add_design_rule). It filed it only as a missing usage class ("an invalid_argument class is owed"), never as a refusal that fails to speak. So this is a recurrence of a phrasing seen 20 days ago.

⑤ MEASURED, reflow2-mcp 0.77.0 --call on a scratch store. Log: /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-C/measure.log. Each case exited 2 with the bare string, and none named the tool or the field:
- external_dependency components:"core" → `invalid type: string "core", expected a sequence`;
- add_decision related_to:"dec:y" → the same shape;
- add_verification verifies:"cap:y" → the same;
- record_finding steps:"get_node" → the same;
- add_requirement name:42 → `invalid type: integer 42, expected a string`;
- add_epoch sequence:"one" → `expected i64`;
- search_design query:[..] → `invalid type: sequence, expected a string`;
- loop_status since_export:"yes" → `expected a boolean`.
CONTROLS: create_edges with an unknown key gets the rewritten "unknown field … expected check_only or edges" plus the hint, and a missing field names tool and field (refusal_speaks passes in CI). THE CLASS IS EVERY TOOL WITH A TYPED PARAMETER.

③④ CODE, origin/main:
- service.rs call_tool: `if text.contains("unknown field") … else if text.contains("missing field") … else None`. Anything else is returned as rmcp built it.
- refusal_speaks.py: "call it with `{}` … Plus one `unknown field` probe". The gate cannot see a type error, because it never sends one.
- usage.rs classes refusals by the same two phrasings, so these land in `other`. That is the 2026-09-12 observation, from the ledger's side.
- bulk_edges.rs:147 alone prefixes "`{tool}`: failed to deserialize parameters", for its per-item errors.
- main.rs call_one_tool prints "reflow2: `{tool}` refused —" only for an Err (exit 1). An isError result (exit 2) is printed bare, so the door's own tool-naming misses exactly this case.

⑥ THE CLASS: the interception matches serde's English phrasings one at a time, as instances. serde_json does not name the failing field for a type error, so the field path is lost unless the parameters are deserialised with path tracking (for example serde_path_to_error) or the refusal is rebuilt from the tool's schema.

UNDER MCP: identical text, because rmcp produces it before any handler. An MCP client knows which tool it called, but still not which field.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether rmcp exposes a hook to deserialise with a path. Only the text-match point was read.
